newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firm but off highs, in range.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firm but off highs, in range.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled firmer but well off the highs amid brisk activity.
Dealers attributed gains to technically-driven local and fund short-covering coupled with a lack of selling, in early activity.
The benchmark May contract climbed to a high of 11.01 cents, where trade selling emerged and knocked the contract towards the middle of the day's range.

Trade scale-up selling was cited at each tick higher from midday and by the close, prices had retreated to their recent trading range, with no sign that they will break out in the near term, market sources said.
The spot month closed up 0.15 cent at 10.90 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.01 to 10.70 cents. The outer months settled 0.11 to 0.06 firmer.
Volume was estimated at 20,109 lots compared to Wednesday's official 19,273 lots.
Open interest in most-active May fell 1,925 lots to 63,601 lots as of Wednesday's close.

Despite today's gains, May closed under the week's high of 10.93 cents reached on Monday. Technically, the contract will need to get above 11.10 to attract more substantial buying, dealers said. Support in May was pegged at 10.68, the low hit March 3.
Fundamentally, there is still not enough physical offtake to jolt the market out of its range, market analysts said.
